issues.body: `_live_children` only models `ast.If` and `ast.While`; every other node falls back to all children even when Python provably does not evaluate them. Consequently `_park_call_site` still returns `dispatch` for a loop such as `for number in (targets if False else []): park_starved_partition_holder(...)`: `_live_nodes(loop.iter)` sees the dead `targets` name, no slice is present, and `_live_nodes(loop)` sees the call, although the loop parks nothing. The same bypass exists with short-circuit expressions such as `[] and targets`. This contradicts the required proof that the production function iterates the returned batch, and it is exactly the dead-code acceptance class this change is intended to close.
issues.fix_hint: Model the relevant expression control flow fail-closed (at minimum `IfExp` and short-circuit `BoolOp` with literal-decidable operands), or make the loop-iterable proof structurally require an unconditionally evaluated path from the bound batch name. Add a live control and named red tests for `targets if False else []`, `[] and targets`, and corresponding live branches so the checker neither accepts dead operands nor refuses valid ones vacuously.
issues.title: Acceptance traversal treats dead conditional-expression operands as live

verdict.summary: The new traversal closes the specific statement-level if/while and nested-callable cases covered by the tests, but it still certifies provably non-running park seams through other Python control-flow expressions. Because this is the acceptance evidence for the production batch seam, that leaves the trust check bypassable and the liveness claim incomplete.
